government.note: Federal parliamentary republic. The President is elected by an electoral college of members of Parliament and of the state legislative assemblies; the Prime Minister is appointed by the President and must keep the confidence of the Lok Sabha. The constitution has no provision for national referendums.

reserved_seats.group: Anglo-Indian community (nominated by the President; abolished from 2020 by the 104th Amendment)

system.note: 543 single-member constituencies elected by first-past-the-post, some reserved for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes, plus 2 nominated Anglo-Indian members until 2020. seats_2000 is the result of the September-October 1999 election (13th Lok Sabha); by-election changes before 1 January 2000 are not modelled.

233 members elected by the state and union-territory legislative assemblies by single transferable vote, one third every two years, plus 12 members nominated by the President. The party breakdown on 1 January 2000 was not found in a fetched source, so all elected seats are recorded as others.

start_2000.ideology_support_note: Derived from 1999 Lok Sabha shares of valid votes: INC 28.3% (social liberal); BJP 23.75% and Shiv Sena 1.56% (Hindu nationalist); CPI(M) 5.4%, CPI 1.48%, RSP, Forward Bloc and CPI(ML) Liberation about 1.1% (Marxist-Leninist); BSP 4.16%, JD(U) 3.1%, RJD 2.79%, JD(S) 0.91% (social democrat); SP 3.76% (left populist); TDP 3.65%, Trinamool 2.57%, AIADMK 1.93%, DMK 1.73%, BJD 1.2%, SAD 0.69%, MDMK 0.44%, National Conference 0.12% (regionalist); NCP 2.27% (centrist liberal); INLD and RLD 0.92% (agrarian); PMK 0.65% (right populist); Muslim League and AIMIM 0.35% (Islamic democrat). The remaining 4.4% for small parties is split between regionalist (2.5 points) and social democrat (1 point) and big tent; independents (2.74%) are counted as big tent.

claims.note: India claims the whole of the former princely state of Jammu and Kashmir, including the areas administered by Pakistan (Azad Kashmir and Gilgit-Baltistan).
India claims Aksai Chin, administered by China, as part of Ladakh (Jammu and Kashmir in 2000).
